Subject: Hosting options — sizing guidance for regulated inference workloads

Neha / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have a procurement window opening in May and need an apples-to-apples comparison between a Private (customer-managed / VPC or on-prem) deployment and Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) for our regulated inference workloads. High level requirements: 
- Peak expected QPS: 12 text-generation requests/sec (avg 120 tokens each) per production service across 3 services (~36 QPS total).
- 95th pct latency SLO: <= 250ms for 32-token responses, 500ms for 256-token responses.
- Data controls: customer-managed VPC and audited access; SOC2 + additional attestation required.
- Traffic pattern: heavy diurnal peaks (1.5x baseline) and occasional burst events (3x for up to 10 minutes).

Can you please provide:
1) Sizing for Private vs Dedicated (GPU type, node counts, expected concurrency, KV cache sizing).
2) Expected differences in unit cost (per-token cost or hourly committed cost) and an OPEX vs CAPEX sketch.
3) Migration/procurement timeline and any gating items (e.g., networking, HSM/KMS support).
4) Any recommended hybrid path (pilot on Dedicated -> migrate to Private) and rollback/fallback suggestions.

We need a short one-pager to share with procurement and security by EOD Friday if possible.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Smith
Head of Platform Engineering | Dealbound AI

Subject: INTERNAL: Draft sizing for Dealbound (36 QPS baseline) — notes and assumptions

Internal summary (working draft) — earliest pass so we can finalize the external memo. Assumptions:
- Workload: autoregressive generation model (7B–13B open model family), typical response 120 tokens, tail usage up to 1k tokens for rare sessions.
- Latency target: p95 <= 250ms (32 tokens) / <= 500ms (256 tokens). 32-token perf drives CPU/GPU warm-up and KV cache behavior.
- Cache: expect high prefix reuse; propose LRU KV cache per model host with 8–16GB of KV per model instance.
- Quantization: we recommend int8/4 quantization where quality permits to reduce memory footprint on A100s and increase concurrency.

Sizing options (approx):
1) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool in our tenancy) — recommended for fastest time-to-value:
   - GPU: H100 80GB (preferred) or A100 80GB if H100 supply constrained.
   - Model shard footprint: whole-model-in-GPU for 13B on H100 with q4_0 ~ 20–28GB effective.
   - Concurrency target: 8 concurrent streams per GPU for 120-token responses at p95 220–260ms.
   - Nodes: target 6 GPUs to meet baseline (36 QPS) with headroom for 3x burst using burst autoscale to 18 GPUs (burst policy 10–15min windows).
   - Expected committed monthly: 6 GPUs reserved; burst billing for additional.

2) Private (customer VPC / customer-managed hardware or Redwood-managed private cluster):
   - For customer-managed on-prem: recommend H100 80GB x 8 nodes (64 GPUs) if they require full air-gapped capacity for 3x burst without cloud-bursting.
   - For Redwood Private in customer VPC (managed compute in their VPC): recommend 12 H100 GPUs (3x baseline) with private control plane and RBAC + KMS integration. This balances cost vs ability to autoscale within VPC.
   - Network: 100Gbps interconnect between hosts; provision for egress between model hosts and KV cache nodes.
   - Expected p95 latency comparable to Dedicated if networking and kernel selection tuned; overhead for private control plane ~10–30ms depending on VPC topology.

Cost notes (high-level):
- Dedicated (6 reserved H100-equivalent GPUs) wins short-term OPEX predictability; lower immediate onboarding than private. OPEX estimate: reserved monthly run-rate (committed) + burst on-demand increments; per-token unit cost ~ lower than on-demand but higher than large CAPEX amortized private if fully utilized.
- Private CAPEX: large upfront (hardware + networking) but lower long-run per-token cost at high utilization; requires ops maturity and procurement lead time (8–14 weeks hardware + integration).

Risk and compliance gating items:
- KMS/HSM integration and key rotation for Private (customer-managed keys) — require security runbook and proof-of-concept for HSM agent connectivity.
- SOC2 and penetration-testing evidence: Redwood can provide SOC2 report and attestation; for private on-prem, customer requested additional evidence for access controls.
- Network egress and private endpoints — must validate procurement firewall rules and allow specific CIDR ranges for control-plane callbacks.

Pilot recommendation:
- Start with a 4-GPU Dedicated pilot (H100-equivalent) configured to mirror production routing rules and KV caching; measure p95/p99 and token cost over 2 weeks with synthetic peak bursts.
- If customer requires private deployment, migrate model artifacts and cache strategy to Private with a staged cutover: shadow traffic -> canary -> cutover. Keep Dedicated as fallback for 60 days.

I’ll put numbers into the spreadsheet and generate a one-pager. Marissa: can you add rough $/month figures for reserved 6-GPU vs 12-GPU private-managed? Karthik: please sanity-check the node counts and networking notes.

— Neha

Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Draft sizing for Dealbound (36 QPS baseline) — notes and assumptions

Adding cost context and commercial pathing:

Cost sketch (ballpark monthly run-rate, USD):
- Dedicated reserved (6 H100-equivalent GPU reservation): ~$225k/month committed (includes reserved discount + baseline networking + instance ops). Burst to 18 GPUs on-demand at ~3x baseline incremental cost.
- Redwood-managed Private in customer VPC (12 GPUs, managed): ~$340k/month run-rate (higher because of dedicated network, private control plane, and managed ops).
- Customer on-prem CAPEX: ~ $2.2M hardware + 20–40% for networking & rack + ongoing ops (~$40k/month ops). Amortized over 36 months ~= $61k/month equivalent (hardware only) — but that assumes 80%+ utilization which is unlikely on early stage usage.

Commercial recommendations:
- Offer a pilot discount for the 4-GPU Dedicated pilot (50% off month 1) and a migration credit if they convert to Private within 120 days. This addresses their procurement risk and shortens procurement cycles.
- Provide a 'fallback SLA' commercial term: if Private deployment experiences latency regressions during the first 60 days, Redwood Dedicated will accept traffic as a fallback under pre-agreed routing policy (technical and billing terms to be documented).

Attachments I will prepare: the latency/SLA comparison PDF (private_vs_reserved_latency_sla.pdf) and a one-page slide for procurement. Also we should include a simple CAPEX vs OPEX tab in the workbook (DB_capex_vs_opex_model.xlsx).

— Marissa
VP, Sales Engineering

- For the pilot we need a one-page SOW and a timeline (ideally a 4–6 week pilot with clear cutover criteria).
- Can you provide a short note on evidence for SOC2 + pen-test for the Private plan? Our security team will want to see specifics (reports, contact for SOC2).

Evan — good questions; short answers and next steps below. I’ve attached the one-pager and worksheet to the shared Drive folder and included the SOW template link (HS-CRM-1873). Attachments: DB_capex_vs_opex_model.xlsx, private_vs_reserved_latency_sla.pdf, dealbound_map_v1.drawio.

Answers: 
- KMS/HSM: supported. For Redwood Private we integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM (support for common KMIP/HSM vendors). We never store plaintext keys; access is enforced through our control-plane RBAC and auditable logs. We will include the KMS integration checklist in the SOW.
- SOC2 + pen-test: Redwood will supply our latest SOC2 Type II report and an execution summary of recent penetration testing. For Private on-prem, we will provide the same artifacts and can coordinate a joint pen-test if required (procurement covers third-party costs).
- Pilot SOW and timeline: propose 4-week technical pilot (week 0 onboarding + week 1–3 run tests + week 4 evaluation and cutover plan). Cutover criteria: p95 latency within 10% of Dedicated pilot and no P1 security issues. We will include fallback routing (Dedicated fallback) and explicit billing credit terms in the SOW.

Action items:
- Marissa: finalize the one-pager and pdf SLA comparison and drop into the Drive folder by Thursday COB.
- Karthik: finalize the Private node-count options (12-node vs 8-node) and add network/topology notes in the draw.io map.
- Tessa/Logan: prepare procurement checklist and SOW template with fallback billing language (we will propose migration credit).
